clue.text: Be frustrated: 'Wake up, love!'

parts.note: to come to is to wake up after passing out
love means nil or nothing in a tennis score

explanation.surface: A frustrated lover pleads with a sleepy partner to wake up.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon and quotation marks make the second half look like speech; it is really two pieces of wordplay, and 'love' is the tennis score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans that fail or fizzle out are thwarted, so to be frustrated is to end in failure with no result.

clue.text: One soldier (highly decorated) about to spring up

indicators.note: one thing about another is wrapped around it, so these letters go round the others

parts.note: something ornate is lavishly decorated
the Roman numeral for one
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A much-medalled soldier is about to leap to his feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highly decorated' suggests medals on the soldier, but it describes a separate word that wraps around the one and the soldier; 'about to' is not a time phrase but the container signal plus the link.
explanation.definitionFit: To originate is to arise or come into being, which is what an idea or custom does when it springs up.

clue.text: Duck seen around English Channel

indicators.note: a thing seen turned around faces the other way, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: Dave is a British television channel
the standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A duck has been spotted near the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English Channel' reads as the stretch of sea, but it splits into two pieces; Dave is a UK comedy TV channel.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck a question or a blow is to dodge or avoid it, the verb sense rather than the waterbird.

clue.text: Imposing tax on Tudor

indicators.note: to tax something is to strain and work it hard, so the letters are pushed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Tudor monarch slaps a new levy on the people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Imposing tax' reads as a single phrase about levies, but 'Imposing' is the definition and 'tax' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Orotund describes a full, grand voice or pompous style, so it means impressive and stately in manner.

clue.text: Old Sky feature raising money for public transport

indicators.note: to raise something is to lift it out of its place, so a letter leaves its slot and moves higher up the column

parts.note: the standard abbreviation for old
M is the abbreviation for money
a nimbus is a rain cloud, a feature of the sky; its M is the letter being moved

explanation.surface: An old Sky TV programme is fundraising for buses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sky' looks like the satellite broadcaster, but it is just the sky, whose cloud is a NIMBUS. In a down answer, raising the M lifts it above the N, turning NIMBUS into MNIBUS, after O for old.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnibus is the full old name for a bus, a road vehicle carrying paying passengers along a fixed route.

clue.text: Punishment advice from Spooner: 'Don't suffer alone!'

indicators.note: Dr Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so his advice arrives with its first sounds exchanged

parts.note: not doing something alone means sharing it; this sound loses its opening 'sh' in the swap
to suffer is to hurt; this sound gains the 'sh' in the swap

explanation.surface: A kindly figure urges a sufferer to confide in others rather than bear pain alone.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the 'sh' and 'h' sounds of 'share hurt' gives the answer. 'Advice' is part of the setup: the quoted words are what Spooner would say.
explanation.definitionFit: A hair shirt was a coarse garment worn as penance, so it stands for self-inflicted punishment or mortification.

clue.text: Mount different part of insect

indicators.note: a different version of a word is made from the same material in a changed arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone mounts a specimen of an insect, choosing a different body part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' sounds like an instruction for pinning a specimen, but it is simply the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The notum is the plate covering the back of each thoracic segment of an insect, a term from entomology.

clue.text: Observe lawyer taking more time to squash start of malicious gossip

indicators.note: squashing something in presses it inside, so one letter is pushed between others

parts.note: to scan is to look over or observe
DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecutor
something taking more time takes longer

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of malicious

explanation.surface: An observer sees a lawyer slowly stamping out a malicious rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Malicious gossip' looks like one phrase; the adjective only supplies its first letter, which squeezes in after the L of LONGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A gossip can be a person who spreads rumours, and a scandalmonger is exactly such a spreader of scandalous tales.

clue.text: Old grids and notes recycled for students of Araucaria?

indicators.note: recycled material is broken down and made into something new, so the letters are reformed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Old crossword grids and notes are recycled for fans who studied under the late setter Araucaria.
explanation.walkthrough: Araucaria was a much-loved Guardian setter, so the surface is about his crossword fans; but the araucaria is also the monkey puzzle tree, and 'and' only joins the two lots of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Dendrologists are scientists of trees, and the araucaria genus includes the monkey puzzle, so they would study it; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: A Tory leader gets personal after feature film involving political corruption

indicators.note: to come after is to follow, so the preceding piece goes first in the line

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature
taken as written

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the first letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of Tory
something personal is your own

explanation.surface: A Conservative leader takes offence at a feature film about sleaze in politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feature film' looks like a single phrase, but 'feature' is a facial feature and 'film' starts the definition. The film is the 1974 Polanski noir about corruption over Los Angeles water.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman Polanski's Chinatown follows a private eye uncovering a corrupt scheme over the water supply to Los Angeles.

clue.text: Foolish eccentric humans — it's how things are

indicators.note: something foolish is silly and senseless, so the letters lose their sensible order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A weary shrug: people are silly and odd, and that is just the way of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' feels like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; 'Foolish' is the signal, and the dash separates the wordplay from the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means given the situation as it stands, so it describes the current state of affairs or conditions.

clue.text: Not suspecting local temperature's dropped

indicators.note: something dropped is let fall and left out, so that letter goes missing

parts.note: a local is a native of the place
T is the abbreviation for temperature, the letter removed

explanation.surface: An unsuspecting resident notices the local temperature has fallen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Temperature's dropped' reads as weather news; it means the T is taken out of the word for a local.
explanation.definitionFit: A naive person is innocent and trusting, unaware of any trickery or deceit around them.

clue.text: Bound to collapse, several inside revealed

indicators.note: a thing inside another sits within it, enclosed by the surrounding letters
a collapsed structure falls apart and its parts land jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
several means some, a few

explanation.surface: A building was sure to fall down, and several people inside were exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' reads as 'certain to', but 'Bound' is the fodder and 'to collapse' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To unbosom is to disclose one's private thoughts or feelings, so the past tense means confided or disclosed.

clue.text: Collected setter's mea culpa to boss?

parts.note: the setter admitting fault would say 'I am an ass', trimmed to its key words
ED is short for editor, the boss of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A calm setter owns up to a mistake in a note to the editor.
explanation.walkthrough: Mea culpa is Latin for 'my fault', an admission of blame; the setter's version is 'am ass'. The boss is the crossword editor, a common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather or accumulate a quantity of something, so the past tense means gathered together.

clue.text: Confused doctor has another look up 'sick at heart'

parts.note: to doctor is to falsify, and to sham is to fake
B is the second option, as in plan B

indicators.note: in a down answer, going up means reading from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: lo is an old word for look

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only the middle letters stay

parts.note: the middle two letters of sick

explanation.surface: A bewildered doctor checks a textbook again, feeling ill at ease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is not a physician but the verb meaning to tamper with. 'Another' as B follows the idea of plan B, the second choice.
explanation.definitionFit: Shambolic is informal British for chaotic and disorganised, so it describes something muddled or in disarray.

clue.text: Brats cycling to party gathering round — go away!

indicators.note: to gather something is to draw it in and hold it inside
a wheel that turns carries its end back to the start, so the last letter moves to the front

parts.note: brats are badly behaved kids
a do is a party
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone shoos away children riding their bikes to a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' looks like bike riding, but it is the signal to move a letter from one end of a word to the other; 'round' is the letter shaped like a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiddoo is dated American slang, as in twenty-three skiddoo, meaning scram or clear off at once.

clue.text: Part of play when Romeo goes — revelatory material

definitions.note: a noun sense: a damascene is damask fabric

indicators.note: whatever goes has left, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a drama scene is one part of a play
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A theatre scene where Romeo exits, and the drama becomes an eye-opener.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo suggests Shakespeare, but here he is only the letter R. A damascene moment recalls Saint Paul's conversion on the road to Damascus.
explanation.definitionFit: A Damascene experience is a sudden conversion or insight; damascene is also a damask cloth, the textile named after the same city.

clue.text: Women in a frenzy talked of Vlad's 'cojones'

indicators.note: something talked of is spoken, so its sound matters rather than its spelling

parts.note: the setter speaking of his own testicles would say my 'nads, slang for gonads, which is what cojones means in Spanish

explanation.surface: Frenzied women gossip about the setter's bravado.
explanation.walkthrough: Cojones is Spanish slang for testicles and, by extension, nerve; Vlad is the setter, so his are 'my 'nads'.
explanation.definitionFit: Maenads were the female followers of Dionysus in Greek myth, known for wild, ecstatic frenzies.

clue.text: Problem: politicians — not ours, Trump principally — invading safe space

indicators.note: invaders enter territory, so these letters go inside the others

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
the African National Congress is South Africa's ruling party, foreign to a British solver

indicators.note: principally means chiefly, and the chief letter of a word is its first

parts.note: the first letter of Trump

explanation.surface: A news complaint: foreign politicians, Trump above all, are intruding on protected spaces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not ours' marks the politicians as a foreign party, here South Africa's. 'Problem' is not the definition but a maths sum.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanctum is a private, sacred or inviolable place where a person is free from intrusion, a refuge.

clue.text: Quick turnover of work force — bar short

indicators.note: something short is missing its end, so the final letter is cut
turning something over flips it end to end, so the string runs backwards

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
the Met is the Metropolitan Police, London's police force
a pub is a bar; its last letter is lost

explanation.surface: High staff turnover at a pub that is always short of workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turnover of work force' suggests staff churn, but the whole string of pieces is flipped. The Met is London's police force.
explanation.definitionFit: Up-tempo describes music played at a fast pace, so it means brisk, lively and fast-moving.

clue.text: Not used — succeeded breaking free

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so one letter enters the other word

parts.note: unpent means not penned in, released
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees

explanation.surface: An escapee succeeded in breaking free without using a thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking free' looks like a phrase about escape; 'breaking' is the container signal and 'free' is the outer word, an old word for released.
explanation.definitionFit: Unspent money or energy has not been expended, so it remains available and untouched.

clue.text: Timeless bonnets as originally described worn at Ascot? They will be

definitions.note: read with the wordplay: they will be worn at Ascot, by the horses

indicators.note: timeless means without time, and time is abbreviated to a single letter to remove
something worn is battered out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: bonnets with its T for time removed
taken as written

indicators.note: originally means at the origin, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of described

explanation.surface: Classic bonnets as described in the fashion pages at Royal Ascot, the famous race meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot suggests hats worn by racegoers, but the answer is worn by the racehorses. 'Worn at Ascot' does double duty as anagram signal and part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A noseband is the part of a horse's bridle passing over the nose, so racehorses at Ascot wear them.

clue.text: Countryman picked up female number 4 on farm?

indicators.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it, so the spoken form is wanted

parts.note: a sow is a female pig, found on a farm
D is the fourth letter of the alphabet, said as dee

explanation.surface: A farm hand hears about a female animal numbered four in the herd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Countryman' suggests a rustic, but it means a man of a particular country. The farm steers 'female' to the pig.
explanation.definitionFit: A Saudi is a native or citizen of Saudi Arabia, so he is a fellow countryman of that nation.

clue.text: Not kosher — I eat hot food unlikely to be this

definitions.note: read with 'hot': hot food is unlikely to be this dish, which is served cold

parts.note: sus is slang for suspect or dodgy
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who cannot eat non-kosher food explains what they eat hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kosher' here means legitimate, so 'not kosher' is dodgy. The whole clue also defines: cold raw fish is unlikely to be hot food.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of cold vinegared rice, often topped with raw fish, so it is rarely served warm.

clue.text: On screen Mr Bean gets a little doolally in car

indicators.note: to get something is to take hold of it, so one piece is taken inside another

parts.note: Sean Bean is a film and TV actor

indicators.note: a little of a word is its smallest opening portion, the first letter

parts.note: the first letter of doolally

explanation.surface: Rowan Atkinson's Mr Bean goes slightly mad in his little car.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Bean suggests the comic character and his Mini, but it means the screen actor whose surname is Bean. Doolally is British slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedan is the American term for a saloon car, an enclosed passenger car with a separate boot.

clue.text: Spain game not international match

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

indicators.note: not means without, so that letter is left out

parts.note: quail is a game bird
I is the abbreviation for international, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A report of a Spain fixture that was only a friendly, not a full international.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' suggests a football match, but it is game in the hunting sense, the bird. 'Match' is the definition, not part of the sports story.
explanation.definitionFit: To match someone is to be as good as them, and to equal them is likewise to rival or be on a par with them.

clue.text: In superlative form, finally attracted interest

indicators.note: to form is to shape material, so the letters are moulded into a new arrangement
finally means at the end, so the last letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of attracted
taken as written

explanation.surface: A performer at the top of their game at last drew interest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In superlative form' looks like a phrase for excellent form, but it splits: 'In' (fashionable) in the superlative is the definition, 'form' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In means fashionable, so its superlative degree is the most fashionable, the most stylish and current of all.
